# Critical integer tilts and affine homothetic captured-cap roots

This note proves a local first-variation identity and its exact consequences
for a finite family of homothetic captured caps. It does not assert that an
arbitrary critical cap has this structure, and it does not resolve (OC).

## 1. First variation for actual proper cuts

Let C be a convex body in R^n x R^d, d >= 2. Let P be the finite set of
integer indices of its nonempty fibers. In this section assume that every
fiber C_z, z in P, has positive d-dimensional volume and that the displayed
cut is proper in every fiber. Write y=(z0,x0), with z0 in P and x0 in C_z0,
and fix a nonzero continuous normal u in R^d. For b in R^n put

    H_b = {(z,x): u.x + b.(z-z0) >= u.x0},
    t_z(b) = u.x0 - b.(z-z0),
    M(b) = sum_z |C_z intersect {u.x >= t_z(b)}|.

Proper means min_{C_z} u.x < t_z(b) < max_{C_z} u.x. Every such hyperplane
has zero d-volume and a section of positive (d-1)-volume. Define

    A_z = H_{d-1}(C_z intersect {u.x=t_z(b)}).

**Lemma 1.** On the open set where all cuts are proper, M is continuously
differentiable, and

    grad M(b) = (1/||u||) sum_z (z-z0) A_z.                 (1)

In particular, if H_b has minimum mass among all closed halfspaces containing
y, or just among nearby integer tilts through y with this fixed u, then

    sum_z (z-z0) A_z = 0.                                 (2)

**Proof.** Use the orthogonal coordinate s=u.x/||u|| and the (d-1)-dimensional
orthogonal complement. For a full-dimensional compact convex body K, its
section-volume function A(s) is positive and continuous on the interior of
its support interval. Here is a direct continuity argument. Fix an interior
level s0 and choose points p_- and p_+ in K at levels s_-<s0<s_+. For s>s0
close to s0, convexity gives the homothetic copy

    (1-lambda)K_{s0}+lambda p_+ in K_s,
    lambda=(s-s0)/(s_+-s0),

so liminf_{s down to s0} A(s)>=A(s0). Conversely, interpolation between K_s
and p_- gives

    (1-mu)K_s+mu p_- in K_{s0},
    mu=(s-s0)/(s-s_-),

and hence A(s)<=(1-mu)^(-(d-1)) A(s0). The analogous argument below s0 proves
continuity. Positivity follows since every interior support level meets the
interior of K: interpolate two interior points on opposite sides of that
level. Fubini now gives the cap-volume derivative -A_z/||u|| with respect to
t_z. The chain rule and the finite sum prove (1). A differentiable function
at an unconstrained local minimum has zero gradient, proving (2). All H_b
contain y on their boundary, so genuine halfspace criticality does give the
required local minimum. This treats oblique halfspaces directly. QED.

The same proof applies if additional fibers are locally wholly captured or
wholly missed: their derivatives are zero. It does not silently extend over
a supporting cut with a positive-area facet. The assumptions above exclude
such a cut.

## 2. Homothetic captured caps convert sections into root weights

Normalize a full-dimensional convex body D in R^d by |D|=1. Suppose that,
at the critical halfspace in Lemma 1, all the actual captured caps have the
form

    K_z := C_z intersect {u.x>=t_z} = a_z D + v_z,
    a_z>0.                                                (3)

Here v_z is a translation vector, not a volume root. The common normal u is
not changed with z. The bottom exposed face

    F = D intersect {u.x=min_D u.x}

has positive (d-1)-volume. Indeed, the bottom exposed face of K_z is exactly
the proper cutting section, and positive homothety in (3) takes F to that
section. Consequently, with A_D=H_{d-1}(F)>0,

    A_z=A_D a_z^(d-1).

Lemma 1 therefore gives

    sum_z (z-z0) a_z^(d-1) = 0.                            (4)

In particular z0 is in the relative interior of conv(P): a convex
combination with a strictly positive coefficient at every point of P cannot
lie in a proper supporting face. Thus an extreme base fiber cannot support
an all-proper critical cap of the form (3), unless P is a singleton.

## 3. Exact budget for affine sampled roots

Assume in addition that these captured-volume roots are affine on all of P:

    a_z = a0 + ell.(z-z0)>0,    a0=a_z0.                  (5)

Write N=|P| and B=sum_z a_z^d, the actual captured mass. Multiplying (4) by
ell gives

    B = a0 sum_z a_z^(d-1).                               (6)

**Theorem 2.** Under (3)--(5),

    B <= N a0^d,                                         (7)

and the exact deficit is

    N a0^d - B
      = sum_z (a0-a_z)^2
          sum_{j=0}^{d-2} (j+1) a0^(d-2-j) a_z^j.        (8)

For d>=2 equality holds exactly when every a_z=a0.

**Proof.** The elementary polynomial identity

    x^d-y^d-d*y^(d-1)*(x-y)
      = (x-y)^2 sum_{j=0}^{d-2}(j+1)x^(d-2-j)y^j

holds for all real x,y; multiplying out proves it by cancellation. Sum it
with x=a0 and y=a_z. The linear terms have sum zero by (6). All terms on the
right are nonnegative, and their inner sums are positive for positive x,y.
This proves every assertion. QED.

Thus the captured mass in the source fiber is at least the average captured
mass over the full finite base. No equality in Brunn--Minkowski for the whole
fibers was used.

There is also a precise formal polynomial optimization statement. Let
E=span(P-z0). On the open convex set

    Omega={eta in E: a0+eta.(z-z0)>0 for every z in P},

put Phi(eta)=sum_z (a0+eta.(z-z0))^d. Its gradient vanishes at eta=ell by
(4), and its Hessian on E is

    d(d-1) sum_z (a0+eta.(z-z0))^(d-2)
                    (z-z0)(z-z0)^T.

It is positive definite, since the vectors z-z0 span E. Thus ell is the
unique minimizer in Omega, and a minimizer over its nonnegative closure.
The latter assertion follows directly from convexity and the zero gradient.
This does NOT identify Phi with actual tilted cap mass solely from (3).
That identification needs the additional geometric persistence hypothesis
in Section 6.

## 4. A complete planar covariance formula

When d=2 the preceding conditions have an explicit solution for arbitrary
finite P, regardless of lattice completeness. Set

    barz = (1/N) sum_z z,
    E = span(P-barz),
    Sigma = (1/N) sum_z (z-barz)(z-barz)^T on E,
    w=z0-barz,    delta^2=w^T Sigma^(-1) w.

If E={0}, use delta=0 and omit the inverse; all the formulas below reduce to
the singleton case. Otherwise Sigma is positive definite on E, because
v^T Sigma v is the average of (v.(z-barz))^2 and these vanish simultaneously
only for v=0 in E.

**Theorem 3.** For d=2, (4)--(5) force

    a_z = alpha [1+w^T Sigma^(-1)(z-barz)],
    a0 = alpha(1+delta^2),
    B = N a0^2/(1+delta^2),                               (9)

where alpha is the positive mean root. Conversely these formulas satisfy
(4)--(5), provided all their displayed roots are positive. In particular,
strict positivity of every bracket is an exact feasibility condition.

**Proof.** Express the affine roots as a_z=alpha+ell.(z-barz). Then

    (1/N)sum_z(z-z0)a_z = Sigma ell-alpha w.

Equation (4) is exactly Sigma ell=alpha w. Evaluating at z0 gives the a0
formula, and averaging the squares gives

    B/N=alpha^2+ell^T Sigma ell=alpha^2(1+delta^2).

The converse follows by substitution. QED.

For P={0,...,N-1}, N>=2, one has

    barz=(N-1)/2,     Sigma=(N^2-1)/12.

The positivity condition is exactly

    |z0-barz| < (N+1)/6.                                  (10)

Indeed the smallest bracket is
1-|z0-barz| ((N-1)/2)/Sigma=1-6|z0-barz|/(N+1).
For even N=2m and the left middle integer z0=m-1,

    delta^2=3/(4m^2-1),
    B=2m a0^2 (4m^2-1)/(4m^2+2).                         (11)

For m>=2 the positivity requirement holds; for m=1 it fails by equality.
With own cap area a0^2=4/9, formula (11) becomes

    B=4m(4m^2-1)/(9(2m^2+1)).                            (12)

In particular m=4 gives 112/33. The separate eight-triangle certificate
proves that this stationary value really is globally critical in that
example. No such global assertion is made here for general m.

## 5. A first-moment expansion budget from actual body convexity

Let r_z=|C_z|^(1/d) denote the WHOLE-fiber volume roots, and write r0=r_z0.
The actual whole-fiber root function on the continuous projection of C is
concave by the ordinary Brunn--Minkowski inequality and the inclusion

    (1-t)C_z+t C_z' subset C_{(1-t)z+t z'}.

The positive weights a_z^(d-1) have barycenter z0 by (4). Their weighted
Jensen inequality therefore gives

    sum_z a_z^(d-1) r_z <= r0 sum_z a_z^(d-1).

Using (6), this is equivalently

    sum_z (a_z^d/B) (r_z/a_z) <= r0/a0.                   (13)

The right side is p^(-1/d), where p=a0^d/r0^d is the source's own captured
fraction. Equation (13) is a first-moment budget with respect to captured
mass. It does not by itself control the d-th moment
sum_z (a_z^d/B)(r_z/a_z)^d, which is the total-to-captured mass ratio.
No such further inference is part of this note.

## 6. When the sampled polynomial is the actual tilt polynomial

The necessary extra hypothesis can be stated exactly. Replace u by a unit
normal, absorbing its length into b. Assume that for each z there is a fixed
apex p_z, a fixed h>0, and an open interval I_z about t_z, such that throughout
I_z the upper cap C_z intersect {u.x>=s} is a cone cap of a common normalized
shape D, with root

    root_z(s) = (u.p_z-s)/h >0.                            (14)

For example, this holds in a simplex while the cutting hyperplane stays
strictly between the unique upper vertex and all other vertices. The common
shape assumption includes the same height h after |D|=1 normalization.
These are hypotheses about the ACTUAL fibers in a neighborhood of the cuts,
not conclusions drawn from homothety at a single cut.

For any small integer tilt delta b keeping every t_z-delta b.(z-z0) inside
I_z, (14) gives the exact identity

    M(b+delta b)
      = sum_z [a_z + delta b.(z-z0)/h]^d.                 (15)

Thus on this tilt cell the polynomial in Section 3 is the actual cap mass.
Its zero-gradient condition is sufficient for a strict local minimum in
all effective integer-tilt directions. Its exact Taylor difference is

    M(b+delta b)-M(b)
      = sum_{k=2}^d binom(d,k) h^(-k)
          sum_z a_z^(d-k) [delta b.(z-z0)]^k,             (16)

where the k=1 term vanishes by (4). Convexity of t^d on positive roots, rather
than the sign of each separate odd Taylor term, proves nonnegativity.
The Hessian is positive definite on E. Nothing here establishes optimality
against continuous-normal changes or against leaving the tilt cell; those
are distinct conditions.

For clarity, homothety of captured caps at a SINGLE cut does not imply the
persistence hypothesis. A planar triangular upper cap can be extended below
its base either along its cone or by a rectangle of the same width. These
are convex bodies locally at the base: the slice widths are respectively
linear on both sides, or constant below and decreasing linearly above.
They have exactly the same selected cap and selected section, but their
second one-sided derivatives under lowering the cut differ. Therefore (15)
cannot be claimed from (3) alone.

Here is an exact version of that distinction. In coordinates (x,s), let

    K_cone = {(x,s): -1<=s<=1, |x|<=1-s},
    K_flat = {(x,s): -1<=s<=1, |x|<=min(1,1-s)}.

Both are full-dimensional compact convex polygons. At s=0 their upper caps
are the same area-one triangle D={(x,s):0<=s<=1, |x|<=1-s}; their cutting
sections both have length two. Take the actual three-fiber bodies
C=[-1,1] x K_cone or C=[-1,1] x K_flat and y=(0,0,0). The halfspace s+bz>=0
has all proper cuts for |b|<1. Its actual captured masses are, exactly,

    M_cone(b)=3+2b^2,
    M_flat(b)=3+b^2.

Indeed the upper-tail areas at threshold t near zero are respectively
(1-t)^2 on both sides, and (1-t)^2 for t>=0 but 1-2t for t<=0.
Thus at b=0 both examples have exactly the same affine cap roots a_z=1,
exactly the same section weights, and a strict integer-tilt local minimum.
Nevertheless their second variations differ. The flat example contradicts
any inference of (15) from selected-cap homothety and first-order tilt
criticality alone. No assertion of globally deepest mixed-integer centers is
needed for this distinction.

## 7. The complete first variation and the source section centroid

The preceding first variation can include the continuous normal as well.
Let c_z denote the centroid, in R^d, of the positive-area cutting section.
For any perturbations delta b in R^n and delta u in R^d, at an all-proper cut
one has

    D M[(delta b,delta u)]
      = (1/||u||) sum_z A_z
          [delta b.(z-z0) + delta u.(c_z-x0)].             (17)

Consequently genuine halfspace criticality through y implies both

    sum_z A_z(z-z0)=0,
    sum_z A_z(c_z-x0)=0.                                  (18)

**Proof of (17).** Translate continuous coordinates by x0 and rotate them so
that the initial normal is kappa e_d, kappa=||u||>0. Write x=(x',s). At a
fixed fiber the old cutting level is s_z=-b.(z-z0)/kappa. Under the joint
perturbation the new cutting graph is

    s = [-b.(z-z0)-epsilon(delta b.(z-z0)+delta u'.x')]
                           /(kappa+epsilon delta u_d)
      = s_z - (epsilon/kappa)
          [delta b.(z-z0)+delta u'.x'+delta u_d s_z]
          + O(epsilon^2),

uniformly for x' in the bounded projection of C_z. The old section is a
full-dimensional convex body in its hyperplane. Except on its relative
boundary, which has (d-1)-measure zero, points x' in that section have
(x',s_z) in the interior of C_z; the vertical fiber therefore contains a
neighborhood of s_z. At such x' the first-order change in captured vertical
length equals the old graph minus the new graph. Outside the closed section,
compactness gives a positive gap at that individual x', so this derivative
is zero. All difference quotients are uniformly bounded by a fixed constant
on a bounded set of x', since the graph displacement is uniformly
O(|epsilon|). Dominated convergence gives the integral of the displayed
linear coefficient over the old section. This is exactly its area times
its centroid expression in (17). Summing the finitely many fibers and
undoing the continuous translation and rotation proves the formula.
The standard elementary convex fact used here is
relint(C_z intersect L)=int(C_z) intersect L when L meets int(C_z): one
inclusion is immediate. For the converse, let p be in the relative interior
of the section and q in int(C_z) intersect L. Choose delta>0 small enough
that p'=p+delta(p-q) still belongs to the section. Then
p=[delta/(1+delta)]q+[1/(1+delta)]p'; interpolating a small full-dimensional
ball about q with p' gives a small full-dimensional ball about p inside
C_z. A convex body's relative boundary has
Lebesgue measure zero, for example by radial comparison with homothetic
copies about an interior point. Hence no regularity of facets or of the
body boundary is needed. At a local minimum all these directional
derivatives vanish, proving (18). QED.

**Corollary 4.** Suppose the critical homothetic caps in (3) have both a_z and
v_z affine in z on P. Then

    x0 = c_z0.                                            (19)

In words, the actual source point is the centroid of its own cutting
section. Indeed, if c_F is the centroid of the common bottom face of D,
then c_z=a_z c_F+v_z is affine in z. The first equation in (18) implies
sum_z A_z c_z=(sum_z A_z)c_z0; the second implies this same weighted sum is
(sum_z A_z)x0. The positive total section area proves (19).

Equation (19) is a section-centroid conclusion. It does not assert that x0
is the centroid of the whole fiber or of its captured cap. Affine cap roots
alone, without affine translations or another reason for affine section
centroids, do not imply (19).
